   8│ # Code investigation procedure
   9│ 
  10│ Goal: understand enough of the real code to change it safely — never edit a file you have not
  11│ read, never assume an API exists without seeing it.
  12│ 
  13│ ## Procedure
  14│ 
  15│ 1. **Orient first.** Read `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, and any `CLAUDE.md` at the root before
  16│    diving in — they often name the entry points and the conventions you must follow.
  17│ 2. **Find by name, then by content.** Use `glob_files` to locate files by path pattern, then
  18│    `search_code` to find the symbols/strings that matter. Search for the *callee* to find all
  19│    call sites; search for the *type name* to find its definition and uses.
  20│ 3. **Read the real thing.** Open the actual files with `read_file`. Page through large files
  21│    with explicit line ranges. Confirm a function's signature and behavior from source — do not
  22│    infer it from its name.
  23│ 4. **Trace the path end to end.** For a behavior, follow it from entry point → the function
  24│    that implements it → its callers and callees. Note every site that shares the pattern you
  25│    intend to change; a fix usually touches more than one.
  26│ 5. **State your model before editing.** Summarize what you found — which files own what, where
  27│    the change must land, and which sibling sites need the same change — then make the edit.
  28│ 
  29│ ## Anti-patterns
  30│ 
  31│ - Editing a file you only grepped and never read.
  32│ - Assuming a helper/method exists because the name "should" be there — verify in source.
  33│ - Fixing the one site that failed while leaving identical sibling sites unchanged.
  34│

  15│ ## Industry standard vs. us, per layer
  16│ 
  17│ ### Isolation / collision-prevention — **we're AT/AHEAD of standard on partitioning, BELOW on sandbox + merge**
  18│ - **Standard:** worktree-per-agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) for collision; **containers/microVMs** (OpenHands=Docker, SWE-agent=Docker, Devin=Firecracker) for untrusted code; **merge queues** (GitHub/Mergify/Graphite) that re-test the *combined* tree before main.
  19│ - **Us:** disjoint write-set leases (stronger than most tools — overlapping non-empty lease is structurally unreachable) + worktree isolation. **Missing: kernel sandbox** (worktree ≠ security; a hijacked agent can `rm -rf`/exfiltrate) and **combined-tree merge queue** (two green agents can break main together — the exact failure the AgenticFlict research documents).

  21│ 
  22│ ### Build trust / provenance — **real defense, wrong crypto primitive, unwired top tier**
  23│ - **Standard:** SLSA levels + in-toto/DSSE attestation format + Sigstore (cosign/Fulcio/Rekor) **signature-based, identity-bound** provenance + transparency log; enforced at deploy (GitHub Artifact Attestations, Kyverno/OPA). AI-specific: TEE remote attestation, tamper-evident agent logs.

  35│ - Sources: GitHub merge queue, Mergify, Graphite stack-aware queue, Argo Rollouts, LaunchDarkly.
  36│ 
  37│ ### Eval integrity / reward-hacking / drift — **strong crude-forgery defense, dead sophisticated defense, neutered drift**

   1│ # Mythos
   2│ 
   3│ **An open-source agent shell that runs on *any* model you bring a key for.**
   4│ 
   5│ Mythos is a terminal-first autonomous coding/agent runtime in the spirit of Claude Code — plan →
   6│ act → observe → repeat, over real tools, in your project — but **provider-agnostic**: point it at
   7│ OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, MiMo, or a local model (Ollama / MLX) with
   8│ your own key. One agent loop, every AI.
   9│ 
  10│ ```
  11│ $ kist "find the slowest test and tell me why"
  12│ $ kist                       # interactive REPL
  13│ $ kist --resume <id>         # pick a run back up where it stopped
  14│ ```
  15│ 
  16│ > **Status: PILOT.** The engine is built, tested (130+ tests), and security-reviewed. It runs real
  17│ > agentic loops against real providers today. It is not yet 1.0 — see [Status](#status).
  18│ 
  19│ ## Why
  20│ 
  21│ Claude Code is excellent and Anthropic-only. Mythos asks: what if the same kind of agent shell were
  22│ **open source** and ran on **whatever model you want** — including local, offline ones? You own the
  23│ keys, the data path, and the code.
  24│ 
  25│ ## Quick start
  26│ 
  27│ ```bash
  28│ # Build the CLI (Swift 5.9+, macOS or Linux)
  29│ swift build -c release            # produces .build/release/kist
  30│ 
  31│ # Bring a key (any one of these works; Mythos auto-picks a configured provider)
  32│ export OPENAI_API_KEY=…           # or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY / …
  33│ kist --list-providers             # see what's configured
  34│ 
  35│ # Run
  36│ kist "summarize what this project does and list its entry points"
  37│ kist                              # REPL: chat, it acts, you continue (/help, /clear, /exit)
  38│ ```
  39│ 
  40│ Local, no key needed: run an [Ollama](https://ollama.com) model and `kist --provider ollama "…"`.
  41│ 
  42│ ## What it does
  43│ 
  44│ | | |
  45│ |---|---|
  46│ | **BYOK, 10 providers** | OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, MiMo (cloud) + Ollama, MLX (local). Keys from Keychain (macOS) or env. |
  47│ | **Real tools, sandboxed** | read / write / edit / list / glob / search, and (opt-in) shell — every path confined to the project root. |
  48│ | **Resume** | every step is checkpointed; `kist --resume <id>` / `--resume-last` / `--list`. |
  49│ | **Self-correction** | live re-plan when actions keep failing. |
  50│ | **Human-in-the-loop** | in the REPL, shell + file-write tools ask before they run (`--yolo` to skip). |
  51│ | **MCP** | use any [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server's tools — configure in `~/.mcp.json`. |
  52│ | **Multi-agent** | the agent can `spawn_agent` to delegate a focused subtask to a fresh sub-agent. |
  53│ 
  54│ ## Safety & privacy
  55│ 
  56│ **No telemetry. No phone-home.** Mythos sends your prompts and code only to the AI provider *you*
  57│ configured, using *your* key — and nowhere else. There's no analytics, no usage beacon, no crash
  58│ reporter; nothing is sent to the maintainers. The only outbound calls are to the provider endpoint you
  59│ chose and the (SSRF-guarded) `fetch_url` tool.
  60│ 
  61│ **A dev tool, not an exploit tool.** Mythos ships no scanners and no attack tooling — it's a general
  62│ coding agent (read / write / edit / search / generate / run). Use it only on systems you own or are
  63│ authorized to work on. Full policy + responsible-use + vuln disclosure: [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md).
  64│ 
  65│ Because it executes tools, confinement is first-class (engine threat model:
  66│ [`Sources/AgentCore/SECURITY.md`](Sources/AgentCore/SECURITY.md)):
  67│ 
  68│ - **Filesystem confinement** — file tools are restricted to the project root via an `openat`/
  69│   `O_NOFOLLOW` layer (`ConfinedRoot`) that defeats `..`/symlink escapes.
  70│ - **SSRF-guarded network** — `fetch_url` resolves the host and **refuses** loopback, private
  71│   (RFC-1918), link-local, and cloud-metadata IPs, and follows no redirects.
  72│ - **Process-group teardown** — spawned commands run in their own process group and are killed as a
  73│   group on timeout/return; no orphaned grandchildren.
  74│ - **Shell off by default** — `run_command` is disabled unless you pass `--allow-shell`; a deny-list
  75│   still blocks the worst shapes; raw shell needs approval.
  76│ - **Opt-in OS sandbox** — `--sandbox` wraps commands in macOS Seatbelt (kernel-enforced network-deny
  77│   + write-confinement). Linux bubblewrap is on the roadmap.
  78│ - **Tool approval** — the REPL prompts y/n before sensitive tools; sub-agents inherit the policy.
  79│ - **Spend ceiling** — `--budget <tokens>` hard-stops a run at the cap (honest-fail, no surprise bill).
  80│ 
  81│ ## Architecture
  82│ 
  83│ Two pieces, one Foundation-only Swift package (`AgentCore`) + a CLI (`Kist`):
  84│ 
  85│ - **`AgentCore`** — the headless, cross-platform engine: pluggable providers (`ChatProvider`),
  86│   sandboxed `ToolRegistry`, an MCP client, and `HeadlessAgentLoop` (the agent loop). No UI deps.
  87│ - **`Kist`** — the terminal shell wired on top.
  88│ 
  89│ The loop is a **provider-agnostic text protocol** (ReAct): the model emits a small JSON action
  90│ object, Mythos parses and dispatches it, feeds the result back, and repeats. Because it relies on
  91│ structured *text* rather than a provider's native tool-calling format, the *same* loop works across
  92│ every provider — including local models with no function-calling. (Native tool-calling as a
  93│ reliability boost on capable providers is on the roadmap.)
  94│ 
  95│ A macOS SwiftUI app shares the same `AgentCore` engine.
  96│ 
  97│ ## Status
  98│ 
  99│ PILOT-quality and honestly labeled — built and reviewed, not yet 1.0. Known gaps:
 100│ 
 101│ - Interrupted-action reconciliation on resume (a tool can re-run if a crash lands between its side
 102│   effect and the checkpoint write).
 103│ - Linux builds (Foundation-only) but is CI-verified only on macOS so far.
 104│ - No native tool-calling path yet (text protocol only); no per-domain network allowlist.
 105│
